newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bridgestone plans lower Japan tyre output for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Bridgestone plans lower Japan tyre output for 1997.

text.p: Bridgestone Corp said on Thursday that it planned to produce 540,000 tonnes of tyres in Japan this year, down from the record high of 560,000 tonnes in 1996.

"We planned a slight decline in tyre output for this year, taking a view that a planned hike in consumption tax from April may slow tyre demand at home," Yoichiro Kaizaki, president of Bridgestone Corp told reporters.
He said, however, that tyre demand since the beginning of this year has been above last year's levels, partly on a rush to buy ahead of the hike in consumption tax.
He said export demand was also strong, backed by the yen's fall against the dollar.
"We are watching whether tyre demand may slip after April," he said.
The company said that its tyre output in overseas markets is expected to rise by about 10 percent for this year from 780,000 tonnes in 1996.
